## INTRODUCTION

*We will be looking at the **Seoul Bike Sharing** dataset. We will be parsing and cleaning the data, creating summaries, and fitting regression models.*

*Loading packages*

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(rsample)
```

*Reading in the dataset*

```{r}
bike_data <- read_csv('HW9/SeoulBikeData.csv', locale = locale(encoding = 'Latin1'))
```

# PART ONE: EDA

## CHECKING THE DATA

*Checking for missingness*

```{r}
is.na(bike_data)
#No NAs!
```

*Checking column types and values within columns*

```{r}
#Checking column types
str(bike_data)

#Checking numeric data summaries
bike_data |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  summary()

#Checking categorical variable unique values
unique(bike_data$Seasons)
unique(bike_data$Holiday)
unique(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)
```

*Converting **Date** column into an actual date*

```{r}
#The Date variable is stored as a character, so we will use dmy() to convert it into the correct format
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  mutate(Date = dmy(Date))

bike_data$Date

```

*Turning character variables into factors*

```{r}
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  mutate(
    Seasons = as.factor(Seasons),
    Holiday = as.factor(Holiday),
    `Functioning Day` = as.factor(`Functioning Day`)
  )

bike_data
```

*Renaming all variables*

```{r}
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  rename(
    date = Date,
    rented_bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`,
    temp = `Temperature(°C)`,
    humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
    wind_speed = `Wind speed (m/s)`,
    visibility = `Visibility (10m)`,
    dew_point_temp = `Dew point temperature(°C)`,
    solar_rad = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`,
    rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`,
    snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`,
    seasons = Seasons,
    holiday = Holiday,
    functioning_day = `Functioning Day`
  )

bike_data
```

*Creating summary statistics*

```{r}
#We calculated the mean, median, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum
bike_data |>
  summarize(
    mean_bikes = mean(rented_bike_count),
    med_bikes = median(rented_bike_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(rented_bike_count),
    min_bikes = min(rented_bike_count),
    max_bikes = max(rented_bike_count)
  )

#We also found these statistics when grouped by the categorical variables
bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarize(
    mean_bikes = mean(rented_bike_count),
    med_bikes = median(rented_bike_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(rented_bike_count),
    min_bikes = min(rented_bike_count),
    max_bikes = max(rented_bike_count)
  )

bike_data |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarize(
    mean_bikes = mean(rented_bike_count),
    med_bikes = median(rented_bike_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(rented_bike_count),
    min_bikes = min(rented_bike_count),
    max_bikes = max(rented_bike_count)
  )

bike_data |>
  group_by(functioning_day) |>
  summarize(
    mean_bikes = mean(rented_bike_count),
    med_bikes = median(rented_bike_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(rented_bike_count),
    min_bikes = min(rented_bike_count),
    max_bikes = max(rented_bike_count)
  )
```

*Because there were no bikes rented on days that **functioning_day = no**, we are going to exclude this level of the **functioning_day** variable.*

```{r}
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  filter(functioning_day != 'No')

bike_data$functioning_day
```

*Summarizing data across hours*

```{r}
#Getting all of the means and sums for the numeric variables
bike_daily <- bike_data |>
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  summarize(
    sum_rented_count = sum(rented_bike_count),
    sum_rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    sum_snowfall = sum(snowfall),
    mean_temp = mean(temp),
    mean_humidity = mean(humidity),
    mean_wind_speed = mean(wind_speed),
    mean_visibility = mean(visibility),
    mean_dew_temp = mean(dew_point_temp),
    mean_solar_rad = mean(solar_rad),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

bike_daily
```

*Recreating basic summary stats and creating plots*

```{r}
summary(bike_daily)
```

## PLOTS

*This is a line graph that analyzes the number of bike rentals over the **date** variable*

```{r}
ggplot(bike_daily, aes(x = date, y = sum_rented_count)) +
  geom_line(color = 'steelblue') +
  labs(
    title = 'Daily Bike Rentals Over Time',
    x = 'Date',
    y = 'Number of Bikes Rented'
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

*This is a scatterplot that analyzes the correlation between the **number of bike rentals** and **temperature***

```{r}
ggplot(bike_daily, aes(x = mean_temp, y = sum_rented_count)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm') +
  labs(
    title = 'Bike Count by Temperature',
    x = 'Temperature',
    y = 'Bike Count'
  )
```

*This is a heatmap that analyzes the density of bike rentals depending on if it was a holiday and the season*

```{r}
ggplot(bike_daily, aes(x = seasons, y = holiday, fill = sum_rented_count)) +
  geom_tile(color = 'white') +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = 'white', high = 'red') +
  labs(
    title = 'Analysis of Density of Bike Rentals by Holiday and Season',
    x = 'Seasons',
    y = 'Holiday',
    fill = 'Number of Bike Rentals'
  )
```

*This is a boxplot that gives the five number summary for the **bike rental count** variable grouped by the **season** variable*

```{r}
ggplot(bike_daily, aes(x = seasons, y = sum_rented_count)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = 'daily Bike Rentals by Season',
    x = 'Season',
    y = 'Total Daily Rentals'
  )
```

*Finding correlations*

```{r}
bike_cor <- bike_daily |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  cor()

bike_cor
```

# PART TWO: SPLITTING DATA

*Splitting the data and naming the split sets*

```{r}
#Splitting data
set.seed(558)
split_data <- rsample::initial_split(bike_daily, prop = 0.75, strata = seasons)

split_data

#Naming the split sets
train_set <- training(split_data)
test_set <- testing(split_data)
```

# PART THREE: FITTING MLR MODELS

*Adding the **weekend/weekday** variable*

```{r}
#Creating the weekday variable for the training set
train_set <- train_set |>
  mutate(weekday = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), 'weekend', 'weekday')))

#Creating the weekday variable for the testing set
test_set <- test_set |>
  mutate(weekday = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), 'weekend', 'weekday')))

train_set$weekday
test_set$weekday
```

*Standardizing data*

```{r}
#Creating a vector with all names of numeric variables
num_vars <- c('mean_temp', 'mean_humidity', 'mean_wind_speed', 'mean_visibility', 'mean_dew_temp', 'mean_solar_rad', 'sum_rainfall', 'sum_snowfall')

#Finding means of all numeric variables
standard_means <- train_set |>
  summarize(across(all_of(num_vars), mean))

#Finding sd for all numeric variables
standard_sd <- train_set |>
  summarize(across(all_of(num_vars), sd))

#Standardizing both testing and training set
for(v in num_vars){
  train_set[[paste0(v, '_std')]] <-
    (train_set[[v]] - standard_means[[v]]) / standard_sd[[v]]
  
  test_set[[paste0(v, '_std')]] <-
    (test_set[[v]] - standard_means[[v]]) / standard_sd[[v]]
}
```

*Fitting first model*

```{r}
#This model includes all standardized numeric variables as well as seasons, holiday, and weekday
model1 <- lm(
  sum_rented_count ~ mean_temp_std + mean_humidity_std + mean_wind_speed_std + mean_visibility_std + mean_dew_temp_std + mean_solar_rad_std + sum_rainfall_std + sum_snowfall_std + seasons + holiday + weekday,
  data = train_set
)
```

*Fitting second model*

```{r}
#This model uses the same variables as model1 and includes interactions between seasons and holiday, seasons and mean temperature, and mean temperature and the rain sum
model2 <- lm(
  sum_rented_count ~ mean_temp_std + mean_humidity_std + mean_wind_speed_std + mean_visibility_std + mean_dew_temp_std + mean_solar_rad_std + sum_rainfall_std + sum_snowfall_std + seasons + holiday + weekday + seasons:holiday + seasons:mean_temp_std + mean_temp_std:sum_rainfall_std,
  data = train_set
)
```

*Fitting third model*

```{r}
#This model takes everything from model2 and adds squared terms for temperature and humidity
model3 <- lm(
  sum_rented_count ~ mean_temp_std + mean_humidity_std + mean_wind_speed_std + mean_visibility_std + mean_dew_temp_std + mean_solar_rad_std + sum_rainfall_std + sum_snowfall_std + seasons + holiday + weekday + seasons:holiday + seasons:mean_temp_std + mean_temp_std:sum_rainfall_std + I(mean_temp_std^2) + I(mean_humidity_std^2),
  data = train_set
)
```

*Finding the best RMSE*

```{r}
#Making an 'rmse' function that can be used on the models
rmse <- function(actual, predicted){
  sqrt(mean((actual-predicted)^2))
}

#Using predict to make objects that can be used in the 'rmse' function
model1_pred <- predict(model1, newdata = test_set)
model2_pred <- predict(model2, newdata = test_set)
model3_pred <- predict(model3, newdata = test_set)

#Using 'rmse' to find the best fit model and putting the results into a tibble
rmse_results <- tibble(
  model = c('Model 1', 'Model 2', 'Model 3'),
  test_rmse = c(
    rmse(test_set$sum_rented_count, model1_pred),
    rmse(test_set$sum_rented_count, model2_pred),
    rmse(test_set$sum_rented_count, model3_pred)
  )
)

rmse_results

#The best model is model3, since it has the lowest RMSE! We will use it to refit the full dataset
```

*Reproducing model and standardization*

```{r}
#Recreating the weekday variable
full_data <- bike_daily |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(weekday = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), 'weekend', 'weekday')))

#Finding the mean for the full data
full_mean <- full_data |>
  summarize(across(all_of(num_vars), mean))

#Finding the sd for the full data
full_sd <- full_data |>
  summarise(across(all_of(num_vars), sd))

#Standardizing the numeric variables
for(v in num_vars){
  full_data[[paste0(v, '_std')]] <-
    (full_data[[v]] - full_mean[[v]]) / full_sd[[v]]
}
```

*Creating the final model*

```{r}
full_model <- lm(
  sum_rented_count ~ mean_temp_std + mean_humidity_std + mean_wind_speed_std + mean_visibility_std + mean_dew_temp_std + mean_solar_rad_std + sum_rainfall_std + sum_snowfall_std + seasons + holiday + weekday + seasons:holiday + seasons:mean_temp_std + mean_temp_std:sum_rainfall_std + I(mean_temp_std^2) + I(mean_humidity_std^2),
  data = full_data
)

#Finding the coefficients and putting them into a data frame
coef_data <- as.data.frame(coef(full_model)) |>
  arrange(desc(coef(full_model)))

coef_data
```
